title: Schur Complements, Static Condensation, and Dirichlet-to-Neumann Reduction
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in linear algebra/numerical analysis/PDE, centered on the claim that interior degrees of freedom may be eliminated while retaining the response needed at an exposed boundary. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that schur reduction is exact admissible forgetting relative to a boundary-response obligation. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: exact block-matrix derivation, sequential-vs-one-shot elimination, and DtN/static-condensation references, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: Poincaré–Perelman as a Boundary Repair Architecture
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in geometric topology/geometric analysis, centered on the claim that flow exposes continuation defects and surgery performs controlled local repair under global proof obligations. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that the proof architecture calibrates defect, monotone witness, admissible repair, and eventual closure without altering Perelman’s theorem. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: Perelman proof dependency map, Ricci-flow/surgery sequence, and monotone quantities, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: Galerkin Projection as Obligation-Preserving Reduction
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in numerical analysis/PDE, centered on the claim that projection may forget degrees of freedom only relative to the quantity, norm, or proof obligation that must survive. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that approximation validity is obligation-relative; reopening the representation is required when later analysis needs distinctions compiled away. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: Galerkin orthogonality, weighted-radial examples, and failure-typed coefficient/flux example, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: Quotient Spaces and Equivalence Relations as Admissible Forgetting
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in algebra/topology, centered on the claim that a quotient deliberately ceases to distinguish objects equivalent under a declared relation. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that forgetting distinctions is exactly ordinary quotient mathematics when an equivalence relation is justified. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: set/group/topological quotient examples, universal property, and unsafe identification counterexample.

title: Stokes’ Theorem as Exact Boundary Transport
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in differential geometry/vector calculus, centered on the claim that bulk differential structure and boundary integral structure are related by an exact transport theorem. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that boundary is literal mathematical structure and the theorem specifies exactly what is transported. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: generalized Stokes statement, divergence/Green specializations, and orientation caveat.

title: Sheaves and Gluing as Local-to-Global Closure
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in topology/algebraic geometry, centered on the claim that local representations form a global object only when overlap and compatibility obligations close. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that gluing gives native mathematics for compatible local realization and failure to globalize. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: presheaf/sheaf distinction, compatible local sections, and failed gluing example.

title: Green’s Identities, Harmonic Extension, and Boundary Determination
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in analysis/PDE, centered on the claim that interior behavior and boundary values or fluxes are linked by explicit analytical obligations. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that boundary data determine an interior only under stated operator, domain, and regularity conditions. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: Green identities, Dirichlet/Neumann examples, and harmonic extension, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: Cohomology as Obstruction
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in algebraic topology/geometry, centered on the claim that locally valid data may fail to admit a global realization and the obstruction can itself be represented. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that some Boundary defects reduce exactly to established obstruction theory rather than new primitives. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: elementary cocycle/coboundary example, gluing obstruction, and claim-scope firewall.

title: Exact Sequences, Kernels, and Cokernels as Loss and Residual
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in algebra/homological algebra, centered on the claim that kernels record what disappears under a map while cokernels expose what remains unreachable downstream. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that loss, survival, and residual obstruction already have exact algebraic forms. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: short exact sequence, kernel/image/cokernel examples, and failure of exactness.

title: Fiber Bundles, Transition Functions, and Holonomy
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in differential geometry/topology, centered on the claim that local descriptions require lawful transition maps and path transport can retain globally meaningful structure. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that representation choice and invariant structure can be separated without treating local coordinates as physical objects. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: bundle atlas, transition cocycle, and holonomy example.

title: Variational Principles and Constrained Optimization as Admissible Variation
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in calculus of variations/optimization, centered on the claim that the admissible variation space determines which candidate changes are lawful and therefore which extrema are meaningful. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that changing admissibility changes the mathematical problem rather than merely its solution. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: constrained extremum, Euler-Lagrange boundary terms, and active-constraint example.

title: Fourier Transform as Representational Transport
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in harmonic analysis, centered on the claim that the represented object may stay fixed while a lawful change of basis makes different structure local or tractable. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that representation change can expose structure without changing the mathematical object. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: time-frequency pair, convolution/product duality, and invertibility and information-loss caveats.

title: The Spectral Theorem as Representation-Aligned Reduction
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in functional analysis/linear algebra, centered on the claim that choosing a representation adapted to an operator converts difficult action into simpler coordinate structure. title: Fixed-Point Theorems as Closure Theorems

title: Homology: Chains, Cycles, and Boundaries
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in algebraic topology, centered on the claim that the boundary operator obeys exact algebraic laws such as boundary-of-boundary equals zero. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: simplicial chain example, boundary operator, and cycle vs boundary.
